The present petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 384/2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Sadhika Jalan, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Courts, Delhi.
2. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 10.07.2016 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
3. No child was born out of the said wedlock.
4. Due to matrimonial differences between the petitioner and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 22.06.2020.
Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against the petitioner.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties submits that during the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement before Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts,

6.

sentences.text: The Petitioner and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by the counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, Insp. Raj Kumar, P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar.

7. The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioner and she has been residing together peacefully with the petitioner in the matrimonial home since 22.04.2022.
She further states that she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
8. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

9. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ... In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

10. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 384/2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Sadhika Jalan, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Courts, Delhi.

11. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 384/2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Sadhika Jalan, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Courts, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
12. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
13. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
AMIT SHARMA, J APRIL 20, 2023/
